pr.title: Replace NullOp::SizeOf and NullOp::AlignOf by lang items.
pr.description:
Part of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/146411

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/119729
Keeps https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/136175 as it involves `offset_of!` which this PR does not touch.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: No source-grounded counterexample pair exists for this PR. The historically incorrect transformation is the pre-fix LowerIntrinsics/CheckNull/CheckAlignment/InstSimplify lowering of `size_of`/`align_of` to `NullOp::SizeOf`/`NullOp::AlignOf` without a language-level `Sized` requirement. For every operand Miri can actually execute, the type is sized, and both the old layout-based `NullOp` evaluation and the new `<T as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE`/`ALIGN` lang-item constants produce exactly the same layout size/alignment. The regression tests (`size_of-dyn-trait*.rs`, `issue-80742.rs`) show the only divergence is on unsized/`dyn Trait` (or layout-failing) operands: there the old path reaches `span_bug!`/a post-monomorphization ICE, while the fixed path is a compile-time E0277 or E0080 error. Neither yields a defined runtime value, so two functions that both pass Miri on identical concrete inputs cannot produce different values for the actual historical rewrite. Producing a runtime difference would require inventing semantics not present in the PR, e.g. assigning a sentinel value to an unsized layout, which is explicitly disallowed.

analysis.summary: Replacing `NullOp::SizeOf`/`NullOp::AlignOf` with lang-item associated consts (`SizedTypeProperties::SIZE`/`ALIGN`) fixes an ICE on unsized types. Before the fix, `LowerIntrinsics` rewrote `size_of`/`align_of` intrinsic calls into `Rvalue::NullaryOp(SizeOf|AlignOf, ty)`, and const-eval assumed the layout was sized. For a `?Sized`/`dyn Trait` type in a const/generic-const context this reached `span_bug!` instead of emitting a normal `Sized` type error. The corrected representation uses unevaluated constants referring to lang items whose trait has a `Sized` supertrait, so unsized operands are rejected by type checking.
analysis.originalLogic: `LowerIntrinsics` handled `sym::size_of | sym::align_of` by pushing `Rvalue::NullaryOp(null_op, tp_ty)` and turning the call into a `Goto`; const-eval, GVN, DataflowConstProp and KnownPanicsLint then read `layout.size.bytes()`/`layout.align.bytes()` directly, with const-eval asserting sizedness via `span_bug!(self.cur_span(), "unsized type for `NullaryOp::SizeOf`"); `CheckNull`, `CheckAlignment` and `InstSimplify` also synthesized the same nullary ops.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong rewrite is lowering `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` (or synthesizing size/align queries) to `NullOp::SizeOf`/`NullOp::AlignOf` without a language-level `Sized` requirement, then evaluating those ops from the layout. This is only equivalent when `T: Sized`; for unsized types the const evaluator hits the `span_bug!` ICE path. The fixed transformation instead creates an unevaluated constant for the `LangItem::SizeOf`/`LangItem::AlignOf` associated const (`<T as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE/ALIGN`), leaving the `Sized` obligation to normal type checking.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR/const-eval contexts containing `size_of`/`align_of`, including generic `?Sized`/`dyn Trait` types, generic const expressions, box allocation (which needs size+align), null-pointer and alignment checks, and layout/query-cycle cases. Includes both sized types (where old behavior agreed) and unsized types (the trigger).
analysis.trigger: An unsized or `dyn Trait` type flows into `size_of`/`align_of` inside a constant/generic-const context (for example the regression test `fn foo(x: A<dyn Send>)`); old lowering turns it into `NullOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf` and const-eval reaches `span_bug!` rather than a `Sized` error.
preconditions: The query is `size_of` or `align_of` (not `offset_of!`, which remains a NullOp and is explicitly out of scope for #136175).
The operand type may be unsized / `?Sized`, or layout computation may cycle or overflow.
The code path is MIR lowering, const-eval, or a pass that synthesizes size/align expressions.
pitfalls: Retaining or reintroducing `NullOp::SizeOf`/`NullOp::AlignOf` after this PR is wrong because those variants are removed from the MIR and public MIR enums; passes must use `Operand::unevaluated_constant` with `LangItem::SizeOf`/`LangItem::AlignOf`.
Do not assume the fix also covers `offset_of!`: the PR states it 'Keeps https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/136175 as it involves `offset_of!` which this PR does not touch.'
The old behavior was equivalent for sized types; the correctness bug is conditional on unsized/layout-failing operands, so a purely sized-type test cannot distinguish old from new semantics.

Diagnostics move to `core/src/mem/mod.rs` and change error classes (new E0277 for unsized types, E0080 for layout cycles/too-big types); old plain-error stderr expectations are not evidence of a wrong replacement pass.

Decoded MIR test files that keep their old names or comments do not prove the replacement pass is incorrect; compare actual assignments (old `AlignOf(T)` versus new `const <T as std::mem::SizedTypeProperties>::ALIGN`).
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites in the box/drop MIR diffs are separate conditions from the size/align representation change and should not be conflated.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI tests under `tests/ui/const-generics/generic_const_exprs/` with `#![feature(generic_const_exprs)]` and `dyn Trait`/`?Sized` operands, asserting E0277 (`the size for values of type ... cannot be known at compilation time`) and no ICE; the PR renames `tests/crashes/119729.rs` to `size_of-dyn-trait-2.rs` and adds `size_of-dyn-trait.rs`/`size_of-dyn-trait-3.rs`. Add layout/cycle and too-big-array tests expecting E0080 plus `stderr-per-bitwidth` where needed. For pass output, use MIR dump checks such as `_0 = const <T as std::mem::SizedTypeProperties>::ALIGN;` and ensure `LowerIntrinsics` no longer emits `SizeOf(T)`/`AlignOf(T)` (the PR deletes those `lower_intrinsics.*` diff files). Also keep box-expression MIR checks showing `exchange_malloc(const <S as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE, const <S as SizedTypeProperties>::ALIGN)`.
evidence: Replace NullOp::SizeOf and NullOp::AlignOf by lang items.
Keeps https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/136175 as it involves `offset_of!` which this PR does not touch.
